overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 25
overview.text: In this lesson, you will solve complex quantitative problems using two distinct approaches: intuitive unit-rate arithmetic and formal algebraic equations. You will discover why algebra provides a powerful, generalized framework when situations become too complex for simple mental math.
outcomes: Investigate a complex quantitative problem by reasoning with rates and numerical tables.
Formulate and solve a linear equation representing the same physical rate situation.
Compare the efficiency, generality, and cognitive load of arithmetic versus algebraic approaches.
overview.teacherInsight: Allow students to initially struggle with the arithmetic unit-rate table. When they construct the algebraic equation $d = vt$, help them realize that algebra is not an extra chore, but a powerful labor-saving tool.

content.html:
The Print Shop Job: Rates vs. Equations

A commercial print shop has 8 printing presses, each printing at a rate of 25 pages per minute. A cookbook printing run requires 120,000 total pages. How long will the job take?

Method 1: Unit Rate Arithmetic
  • Combined rate = $8 \times 25 = 200\text{ pages/min}$.
  • Pages per hour = $200 \times 60 = 12,000\text{ pages/hr}$.
  • Time = $\frac{120,000}{12,000} = 10\text{ hours}$.
Method 2: Algebraic Formula
  • Let $t$ = time in minutes.
  • $8 \times 25 \times t = 120,000$
  • $200t = 120,000 \implies t = 600\text{ min} = 10\text{ hr}$.

vocabulary.definition: A rate in which the second quantity in the comparison is one unit (e.g., 25 pages per minute).
The total operational output rate achieved when multiple independent agents or machines work concurrently.
A mathematical representation using variables and operations to simulate real-world behaviors and make predictions.

practiceQuestions.question: A print shop operates 8 printing presses, each printing 5,000 pages per hour for 6 hours per day. How many total pages do all 8 presses produce in 2 full operating days?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
From the official Eureka Math Exit Ticket Key:
1 press prints: $5,000\text{ pages/hr} \times 6\text{ hrs/day} = 30,000\text{ pages/day}$.
8 presses print: $8 \times 30,000 = 240,000\text{ pages/day}$.
In 2 days: $2 \times 240,000 = 480,000\text{ pages}$.

practiceQuestions.question: If 1 individual press runs for 2 days on cookbooks while 8 presses run on other jobs, how many pages does that single press produce?
practiceQuestions.explanation: 1 press in 2 days prints $30,000\text{ pages/day} \times 2\text{ days} = 60,000\text{ pages}$.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 25 Exit Ticket: Solving Problems in Two Ways—Rates and Quantities
exitTicket.prompt: Suppose a print shop has 8 printing presses and each runs at 5,000 pages per hour for 6 hours a day. Compute total pages printed for a cookbook job and novel job where 8 presses run for 2 days on novels while 1 press runs for 2 days on cookbooks. Ratio of pages is 2:1.
exitTicket.solution:
1 press in 1 day prints: 5,000 * 6 = 30,000 pages.
8 presses in 1 day: 8 * 30,000 = 240,000 pages.
In 2 days, 8 presses print: 480,000 pages for novels.
1 press in 2 days prints: 60,000 pages for cookbooks.
Total printed: 480,000 + 60,000 = 540,000 pages.
Ratio 2:1 gives 360,000 novel pages and 180,000 cookbook pages.

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Solving Rates Problems in Two Ways — Arithmetic vs. Algebra
guidedExercises.problem: A cyclist rides from Town A to Town B at an average speed of $15\text{ mph}$ and returns along the same route at $10\text{ mph}$. The round trip takes 5 hours total. Solve for the distance $d$ between the towns in two ways: 1) using algebraic equations, and 2) using rate-ratio unit reasoning.
guidedExercises.scaffolding: Method 1: Total time is $t_1 + t_2 = 5$, where $t = \frac{d}{r}$. Method 2: The ratio of speeds is $15:10 = 3:2$, so the ratio of times spent must be inverse ($2:3$).

steps.label: Method 1: Algebraic equation
steps.explanation: Sum of outward time and return time is 5 hours.

steps.label: Method 2: Ratio unit reasoning
steps.math: \text{Speed ratio } 3:2 \implies \text{Time ratio } 2:3 \implies \text{Outward: } 2\text{ hrs}, \text{ Return: } 3\text{ hrs} \implies d = 15(2) = 30\text{ miles}

guidedExercises.commonPitfall: Averaging the two speeds as $\frac{15 + 10}{2} = 12.5\text{ mph}$. Average speed over a round trip is total distance divided by total time: $\frac{60\text{ miles}}{5\text{ hours}} = 12\text{ mph}$, NOT $12.5\text{ mph}$!

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Solve age and rate problems using arithmetic tape diagrams and formal algebraic equations.

problems.prompt: In 16 years, Pia's age will be twice her age 12 years ago. Find Pia's present age using both a tape diagram and an algebraic equation.
problems.solution:
Let p = Pia's present age.
In 16 years: p + 16.
12 years ago: p - 12.
Equation: p + 16 = 2(p - 12)
p + 16 = 2p - 24
40 = p.
Pia's present age is 40 years old. Verification: In 16 years she will be 56; 12 years ago she was 28; 56 is twice 28.

problems.prompt: A printing shop has 8 presses printing 5,000 pages/hr for 6 hrs/day. If 2 presses are taken offline for maintenance, how many total pages can the remaining presses produce in 3 days?
problems.solution:
Remaining presses = 8 - 2 = 6 presses.
Daily output per press: 5,000 \times 6 = 30,000 pages.
Total for 6 presses in 1 day: 6 \times 30,000 = 180,000 pages.
Total in 3 days: 3 \times 180,000 = 540,000 pages.
